correctness.rationale: For non-scalar residue matrices one matrix coordinate is a unit, forcing every commutant to be an R-linear polynomial in that matrix and giving q^(2d+2). For scalar residue matrices, the radical square-zero hypothesis turns commutation into d simultaneous k-linear centralizer equations. A non-scalar 2x2 matrix has a 2-dimensional commutant k[I,T], and distinct such commutants intersect in scalars. The resulting tuple partition supplies the other three strata. Independently count commuting lifts of each commuting residue pair: scalar-scalar pairs have q^(8d) lifts and all other pairs q^(6d) lifts; this matches the sum over the centralizer spectrum. Exhaustive direct pair enumeration checked 16,777,216 matrix pairs for q=2,d=2 and 65,536 pairs each for the characteristic-2 dual numbers and Z/4Z; exact multiplicities and total pair counts agreed. No finite check is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim excludes the known principal d=1 case. The full-text Section 10 of Prasad-Singla-Spallone reduces nonprincipal similarity to a tuple-orbit problem but does not enumerate the four centralizer-size strata or give the q^-6 limiting law. Explicit recent published matrix commuting-graph results are confined to chain rings; affine monoid centralizers count different objects; nonprincipal matrix square-zero enumerations treat X^2=0, not XY=YX. No exact equivalent or stronger cover was found in the actual published-finding corpus searches or inspected primary material; the possibility of a broader implicit equivalence remains recorded.
residual_risks: A historical theorem about centralizers or orbit stabilizer cardinalities for all square-zero local coefficient rings could imply the same four-row count under alternative language.
The general orbit-reduction theorem of Prasad-Singla-Spallone is structurally broader, but obtaining this exact census from it requires additional counting.
An independent publication-priority check and independent proof review have not been performed.

value.rationale: The full-matrix centralizer spectrum is a natural ring invariant, and d=2 is a structural threshold where a genuinely new scalar-only common-commutant stratum emerges. The exact q,d-independent-of-ring-formulas extend the principal case to all nonprincipal square-zero local rings (including mixed characteristic) without requiring a wild classification of matrix tuples. The positive limiting commuting probability q^-6 and conditional concentration on scalar reductions are non-obvious structural consequences, potentially useful in commuting-graph and local-matrix representation problems. The contribution is neither a one-off table nor just an arithmetic normalization.
